Title: Barber Cello Concerto; Leonard Rose "live" NY Philharmonic, Leonard Bernstein, conductor Jan 1959
Description:
This is the only performance that exists of Leonard Rose performing Samuel Barber's 1945 cello concerto. The work, gaining some popularity today, was neglected for decades by the leading cellists of the era. It is a difficult work
that is nevertheless rewarding for both cellist and audience. Rose and Bernstein feed it energy, excitement and love.

Title: Bernstein conducts Britten "Spring Symphony" - LIVE!
Description:
From a 1963 performance at Philharmonic Hall in New York, here is Leonard Bernstein conducting the "Spring Symphony" by Benjamin Britten.  The soloists for this performance were Jennifer Vyvyan, Regina Sarfaty, and Richard Lewis; with the Boys' Choirs from The Little Church Around the Corner and St. Paul's Church of Westfield, NJ (unfortunately not credited in the video itself); the Collegiate Chorale; along with the New York Philharmonic Orchestra.

Part 1
1. Introduction: Shine Out (George Chapman)
2. The Merry Cuckoo (Edmund Spenser)
3. Spring, the Sweet Spring (Thomas Nashe)
4. The Driving Boy (George Peele, John Clare)
5. The Morning Star (John Milton)

Part 2   17:30 
6. Welcome, Maids of Honour (Robert Herrick)
7. Waters Above! (Henry Vaughan)
8. Out on the lawn I Lie in bed (W. H. Auden)

Part 3   29:16 
9. When will my May Come? (Richard Barnfield)
10. Fair and Fair (George Peele)
11. Sound the Flute! (William Blake)

Part 4   35:15 
12. Finale: London, to Thee I do Present (John Fletcher; closing words from ''The Knight of the Burning Pestle'' by Francis Beaumont)

Title: Jean Sibelius - Symphony no. 5: Leonard Bernstein conducting the LSO in 1975
Description:
In late 1966, Leonard Bernstein conducted the London Symphony Orchestra, led by John Georgiadis at Croydon's Fairfield Halls, in Sibelius' fifth symphony. This upload is not of that performance, which is available separately on YouTube. 

Nine years later on 10 September 1975, Bernstein again conducted Sibelius 5 with the LSO, this time led by John Brown, at the Edinburgh Festival. Simultaneously broadcast on television in the UK four days later, this is the radio transmission of that 1975 performance.

1. Tempo molto moderato – Allegro moderato 0:00
2. Andante mosso, quasi allegretto 14:18
3. Allegro molto – Misterioso 23:43

Title: Leonard Bernstein - Symphony no. 2: Leonard Bernstein conducting the LSO in 1986
Description:
Today is the hundredth anniversary of Leonard Bernstein's birth, and as I upload this, the LSO is performing Bernstein's 'On The Town' at the BBC Proms on 25 August 2018. This 1986 performance of Bernstein's second symphony under the composer's direction and featuring Krystian Zimerman as piano soloist at the Barbican was re-mastered today from the original Dolby C cassette recording, and presented in tribute to one of the true geniuses of the twentieth century.

Title: Mahler's Second: Bernstein, Cleveland Orchestra, live in 1970
Description:
Gustav Mahler. Symphony no. 2 in C minor “Resurrection.”
Lorna Haywood, soprano; Christa Ludwig, mezzo-soprano; Blossom Festival Chorus; Margaret Hillis, director; Cleveland Orchestra; Leonard Bernstein, conductor.
Recorded live at Blossom Music Center, Cuyahoga Falls, OH, 9 July 1970.

This was Leonard Bernstein’s only appearance with the Cleveland Orchestra. The music critic Robert Finn called it “quite simply, one of the greatest occasions in Blossom’s history and perhaps in that of the orchestra itself.”

I. Allegro maestoso (0:00) - Im Tempo nachgeben (2:50) - Wie zu Anfang (3:52) - Sehr mässig und zurückhaltend (6:35) - Schnell (11:57) - Tempo I (15:38) - Zurückhalten (17:22) - Tempo sostenuto (19:53) [several beats are clipped off a few measures from the end]

II. Andante moderato (23:13) - Nicht eilen. Sehr gemächlich (25:04) - In Tempo I. zurückkehren (26:51) - Tempo I. Energisch bewegt (29:01) - Wieder ins Tempo zurückgehen. Tempo I (31:20)

III. In ruhig fließender Bewegung (35:31) - Vorwärts (39:25) - Sehr getragen und gesangvoll (40:20) - Zum Tempo I. zurückkehren (41:39) - Tempo I (42:01) - [Lead-up to the “Cry of Despair”] (43:40)

IV. Urlicht. Sehr feierlich, aber schlicht (46:19)

V. Im Tempo des Scherzo. Wild herausfahrend (52:03) - Langsam (53:50) - Im Angang sehr zurückgehalten (57:32) - Wieder sehr breit (58:42) - Rit.-Molto riten.-Maestoso. Sehr zurückhaltend (1:02:08) - Kräftig (1:03:07) - Wieder zurückhaltend (1:06:06) - Langsam (1:08:12) - Der große Appell. Sehr langsam und gedehnt (1:09:47) - Langsam. Misterioso: “Aufersteh’n” (1:12:20) - Etwas bewegter (aber nicht eilen): “O glaube” (1:19:49) - Mit Augschwung, aber nicht eilen: “O Schmerz! Du Alldurchdringer!” (1:22:58)
